name: web_crawler_search_engine
spec: Create an asynchronous web crawler and full text search engine in Python using only the standard library. The system crawls websites starting from seed URLs, builds an inverted index with TF-IDF scoring, and exposes search results through both a REST API and a generated HTML interface. The crawler must respect robots.txt, handle errors gracefully, and support configurable depth and concurrency limits.
features: Reads seed URLs from a plaintext file with one URL per line specified via --seeds flag
Crawling depth is configurable via --depth flag defaulting to 2
Maximum number of pages to crawl is configurable via --limit flag defaulting to 100
Number of concurrent crawler workers is configurable via --workers flag defaulting to 5
Concurrency is implemented using threading with a thread pool and a shared work queue protected by locks
Fetches each URL using urllib from the standard library with a configurable timeout
Parses HTML content using html.parser from the standard library
Extracts all anchor href links from each page and adds discovered in-scope URLs to the crawl queue
Normalizes URLs by resolving relative URLs to absolute, stripping fragments, and deduplicating
Fetches and parses robots.txt for each domain before crawling any page on that domain
Obeys Disallow rules and Crawl-delay directives from robots.txt with per-domain rate limiting
Extracts visible text content from HTML stripping all tags, scripts, and style content
Builds an inverted index mapping stemmed terms to the set of documents containing them with term frequency counts
Computes TF-IDF scores for ranking search results across the crawled corpus
Applies basic text normalization including lowercasing, punctuation removal, and stopword filtering
The inverted index is persisted to disk as a JSON file after crawling completes
The index can be loaded from disk without recrawling via --load-index flag pointing to an existing index file
A REST API server starts on a configurable port after crawling when --serve flag is provided
GET /search?q=query returns a JSON array of results ranked by TF-IDF score each containing title, url, score, and a text snippet
GET /search?q=query&limit=N limits the number of results returned
GET /stats returns JSON containing total pages crawled, total unique terms indexed, index size in bytes, and crawl duration
GET /crawl triggers a new crawl run asynchronously using the original seed file and returns a JSON object with a job_id
GET /crawl/{job_id} returns the current status and progress of a crawl job including pages crawled so far
Generates a static search.html file in the current directory containing a search box that queries the REST API and renders results dynamically using JavaScript fetch
The HTML interface displays each result with a clickable title link, the URL, the TF-IDF score, and a text snippet with query terms wrapped in bold tags
Handles HTTP errors, connection timeouts, SSL errors, and malformed HTML gracefully logging one error line per failed URL
Detects and skips non-HTML content based on the Content-Type response header
Displays a live crawl progress line in the terminal updating in place showing pages crawled, queued, failed, and current URL
Prints a summary report after crawling showing total pages, total terms, top 10 most linked domains, and elapsed time
